🔻 PSG vs Roma: Predicted lineups, team news, and Champions League preview

📌 PSG vs Roma: predicted lineups, injury updates, Champions League statistics, recent form, kick-off time, and everything you need to know ahead of the match.

Paris Saint-Germain will attempt to extend their flawless Champions League campaign when they welcome Roma to the Parc des Princes. The defending European champions have won all four of their league-phase matches, scoring a record-breaking 20 goals, and could establish another milestone in European football against Gian Piero Gasperini's side.
​
Roma arrive in the French capital with considerable attacking momentum following a 5-1 victory over Parma, inspired by four goals from Donyell Malen. However, their inconsistent European performances remain a concern. PSG, meanwhile, must cope with the absence of Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia as Luis Enrique's side seek a 13th consecutive victory across all competitions.
​
Both managers have several selection decisions to consider ahead of Wednesday's meeting, with injuries affecting both squads.
​
PSG predicted XI: Safonov, Hakimi, Zabarnyi, Pacho, Hernandez, Neves, Vitinha, Ruiz, Akliouche, Mayulu, Fran.
​
Roma predicted XI: Vazquez, Mancini, Balerdi, Hermoso, Molina, Cristante, De Roon, Wesley, Soule, Mora, Malen.
​
Luis Enrique has suffered another significant setback in attack after Désiré Doué sustained an anterior cruciate ligament injury during PSG's victory over Nice. The French forward is set to miss the remainder of the season, joining Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the long-term injury list.
​
Doué's absence represents a considerable loss for the European champions. Having registered 45 shots and created 31 chances, he has been one of PSG's most dangerous attacking players.
​
Alessandro Longani is also sidelined with a thigh injury, although the recent return of Ousmane Dembélé provides Enrique with additional attacking options.
​
Fabian Ruiz is expected to feature in midfield after contributing directly to goals in each of his last four Champions League appearances, including scoring in his two most recent matches.
​
Gasperini received a welcome boost during the international break as Paulo Dybala and first-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar returned from injury. Lorenzo Pellegrini, however, remains unavailable with a thigh problem.
​
Devyne Rensch is struggling with an adductor injury, while Leonardo Balerdi is doubtful after suffering an ankle problem.
​
Brazilian wing-back Wesley has strengthened his case for a starting place after providing three assists against Parma, despite only entering the match in the second half.
​
Donyell Malen is expected to spearhead Roma's attack. The Dutch forward leads the Serie A scoring charts with 12 goals and has scored in each of his last three Champions League appearances.
​
Roma injured and doubtful players:
​
Paris Saint-Germain will face Roma on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the Parc des Princes in Paris. The UEFA Champions League Matchday 5 encounter is scheduled to kick off at 8 pm GMT (9 pm CET and 3 pm EST).
​
Swedish referee Glenn Nyberg will oversee the Champions League encounter at the Parc des Princes. He will be assisted by fellow Swedish officials Mahbod Beigi and Andreas Söderkvist, with Adam Ladebäck serving as fourth official.
​
Germany's Bastian Dankert and Poland's Tomasz Kwiatkowski will be responsible for video assistant refereeing duties.

🧠 Why do traders close winning positions too soon?

Cutting profitable trades short can bring your average win close to, or even below, your average loss. That can make consistent profitability harder to achieve.

The urge to exit may come from fear of regret. If your open profit disappears, you might blame yourself for not taking it. Closing the position offers quick relief, but it may be a way to avoid the discomfort of holding.

Before your next trade, picture yourself choosing to hold or close. Ask whether fear of losing your unrealized profit is driving the decision.

To practise, split your planned position into two parts. You can close one and keep the other open, building your comfort with holding winners gradually. This does not eliminate risk.

⚡️ Iran repairs more than 40,000 homes damaged in recent war

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran has repaired more than 40,000 residential units damaged during the recent US-Israeli-imposed war, with nearly 20,000 volunteer groups taking part in the reconstruction effort, says the head of the county’s Basij Organization.

Speaking to IRNA on Wednesday, Brigadier General Mohammad Zahraei said the organization was also pursuing plans to plant 48 million trees and build solar power plants as part of its wider development and reconstruction activities.
​
He said solar power facilities were planned for land and military bases belonging to the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC), adding that the projects would help secure electricity supplies for IRGC facilities during power outages and strengthen passive defense capabilities.
​
The solar projects could also help reduce the country’s electricity imbalance, he said.
​
Zahraei said the recent war had caused damage to public facilities and residential properties among other sites.
​
He cited nearly 53,000 residential units damaged in Tehran, 12,300 in Isfahan and 2,300 in Qom, highlighting the scale of the impact on civilian housing.
​
More than 40,000 of the damaged homes have so far been repaired through the participation of volunteer groups, known as jihadi groups, he said.
​
Nearly 20,000 such groups contributed to the restoration work, demonstrating the scale of public participation in the reconstruction campaign.
